title: China Forced Meta to Reverse a $2 Billion Deal  #meta   #manusai
description:
When Meta acquired Manus for $2 billion, founder Xiao Hong thought it was the biggest moment of his life.

The deal was closed. The money was transferred. The team had already moved.

Then Beijing stepped in.

Investigations. Travel restrictions. State intervention.

And eventually, the entire deal was reportedly reversed.

This isn't just the story of one AI founder. It's a story about the growing AI rivalry between China and the United States, the race for technological dominance, and why governments are treating AI talent like a strategic national asset.

As the gap between the US and China narrows, the stakes are becoming enormous.

Would you stay and build or find a way out?

top_comments.text: The fascinating part nobody's saying out loud is you can reverse a deal on paper, but you can't unlearn what Meta's engineers absorbed in six months of access. Equity and equipment go back but model weights and know how don't. So even a full reversal probably isn't one. The real question is what that does to the value of any China rooted AI startup going forward.
